title: Federal-question jurisdiction
summary: Federal-question jurisdiction concerns actions arising under federal law within the applicable jurisdictional grant. Federal creation of the cause of action supplies the principal route, while a narrow category of state-law claims can also qualify.
notes: A federal defense or a federal issue somewhere in the dispute is not enough by itself. Shoshone and the embedded-issue cases show why the source and nature of the claim must be examined carefully.

sections.Meaning: Federal-question jurisdiction concerns actions arising under federal law within the applicable jurisdictional grant. Federal creation of the cause of action supplies the principal route, while a narrow category of state-law claims can also qualify.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the claim as it appears in a properly pleaded complaint. Ask whether federal law creates the claim, and separately whether a necessary embedded federal issue meets Grable and Gunn. Confirm the particular statute, including any specialized grant.
